questions.stem: What is the key difference between nuclear fission and nuclear fusion?

options.text: Fission releases energy but fusion absorbs energy
Fission uses hydrogen; fusion uses uranium
Fission splits large nuclei; fusion joins small nuclei
Fission occurs in stars; fusion occurs in power stations

questions.explanation: Fission is the splitting of a large nucleus into smaller ones, while fusion is the joining of small nuclei to form a larger one. Both processes release energy.

questions.stem: Which type of radiation is stopped by a sheet of paper?
questions.explanation: Alpha particles are stopped by a sheet of paper or a few centimetres of air. Beta is stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium, and gamma is only significantly reduced by thick lead or concrete.

questions.stem: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 2 days. What fraction of the original nuclei remain after 6 days?
questions.explanation: 6 days = 3 half-lives. After each half-life, half the nuclei remain: 1 -> 1/2 -> 1/4 -> 1/8. So after 3 half-lives, one eighth of the original nuclei remain.

questions.stem: What defines which element an atom is?
questions.explanation: The number of protons (atomic number) defines which element an atom is. Changing the number of protons changes the element. Changing neutrons creates isotopes of the same element.

questions.stem: In a nuclear reactor, what does the coolant do?

options.text: It transfers heat energy away from the reactor core to produce steam for generating electricity
It provides the fuel for fission

questions.explanation: The coolant (often water or carbon dioxide gas) flows through the reactor core, absorbing heat produced by fission. This heat is used to produce steam, which drives turbines connected to generators.

questions.stem: Why is nuclear waste a significant challenge for nuclear power?

options.text: Because high-level waste remains dangerously radioactive for thousands of years and must be stored safely
Because it can only be stored in space
Because it is too heavy to move

questions.explanation: High-level nuclear waste contains isotopes with very long half-lives and remains dangerously radioactive for thousands of years. It must be stored securely, often deep underground, which is expensive and controversial.

questions.stem: Which equation relates mass and energy in nuclear reactions?
questions.explanation: Einstein's equation E = mc squared shows that mass and energy are equivalent. In nuclear reactions, a small loss of mass is converted into a very large amount of energy because c (the speed of light) is an enormous number.
